implementation_notes: NestJS supplies the structure: @Injectable() service classes are providers registered in a module's providers array and injected through the constructor, with the container resolving the whole graph at boot; the operation's unit of work is Prisma's interactive transaction, prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => ...), whose callback commits on return and rolls back on throw. The classic service class is standardised rather than replaced - the decorator plus constructor injection takes over the wiring the classic form did by hand - and a shared transaction client can be propagated to repositories through AsyncLocalStorage when nesting must join automatically. Without a framework the same design is a module of operations plus a withTransaction helper, which stays the simpler choice until several modules must share one provider graph.
pitfalls: Calls made with this.prisma instead of the callback's tx client run outside the transaction - thread the tx parameter into every collaborator.
Nest providers are singletons by default: request-scoped state (tenant, request id) needs Scope.REQUEST or AsyncLocalStorage, not a constructor field.
Interactive transactions hold a database connection for their whole duration; keep external HTTP calls and slow work outside the callback.
